title: Authored CODING_GRAPH literal, `bober pge` CLI, and the committed checksummed topology artifact
description: Author the shipped coding pipeline as a plain typed object literal (export const CODING_GRAPH: TopologySpec) covering every node in the architecture blueprint — research subgraph, planner with clarification loop, supervisor, sprint subgraph, gates, routers, evaluation, synthesis, documenter, gated commit, graceful failure and context compaction. Add the `bober pge` CLI with dump, validate and hash verbs, and commit the serialized artifact to .bober/topology/coding.json so it becomes the load-bearing contract the runtime will later read. Proves topology/content separation: a prompt edit leaves the checksum untouched, an edge addition changes it, and swapping model profiles produces an identical hash.

successCriteria.description: src/pge/topology/coding.graph.ts exports CODING_GRAPH typed as TopologySpec, it parses through TopologySpecSchema, and validateTopology in structural mode returns ok:true with zero error-severity diagnostics.

The authored graph contains every node named in the architecture mermaid blueprint, asserted by a pinned node-id list covering the research, plan, sprint, evaluation, terminal and context-compaction regions, so a silently dropped node fails the test.

`bober pge dump` writes .bober/topology/coding.json containing graphId, graphVersion matching the semver pattern, provenance 'authored', every node id, every node kind and every edge, and the file parses back through TopologySpecSchema.
`bober pge dump --check` exits 0 when the committed artifact matches the canonicalised literal byte for byte and exits non-zero after a single-character mutation of the committed file.
`bober pge validate` exits non-zero and prints the diagnostic code name for each of the 30 malformed fixtures from sprint 1, and exits 0 for the committed artifact.
A test substitutes a spy for every node executor lookup and asserts zero invocations across dump, validate and hash, complementing the sprint-1 lint boundary with a behavioural assertion.
Mutating a prompt body under the prompt store and recomputing `bober pge hash` leaves the topology checksum unchanged, while adding one edge to the literal changes it.

Running dump under two different model configurations produces identical topology checksums while the resolved model ids recorded for the run differ, proving a model-profile swap is not a structural change.

checksumTopology recomputed from the committed artifact's canonicalised node and edge list equals the checksum field stored in that artifact, and a stale checksum surfaces as the ChecksumStale diagnostic rather than silently passing.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors and the full Vitest suite is green.

nonGoals: Do not implement any node body, node registry or executor — this sprint produces data and a reader, nothing runnable.
Do not add render, diff, docs or audit-state verbs to the CLI; sprint 3 owns them and adding stubs now creates dead command surface.
Do not call EffectRegistry.seal() from dump in this sprint — the registry does not exist yet, and importing it would violate the sprint-1 boundary. Sprint 5 adds the seal call.
Do not add .bober/topology/ to .gitignore — this directory is deliberately version-controlled.
Do not change pipeline.engine, the engine seam, or any orchestrator file.
stopConditions: The committed artifact round-trips: literal to canonical form to file to parse to identical checksum.
`bober pge dump --check` fails on a mutated artifact and passes on an untouched one.
A node in the architecture blueprint cannot be expressed under the sprint-1 schema without widening Goto to accept an arbitrary node id, which ADR-3 forbids.
Authoring the literal would require importing a runtime module.
definitionOfDone: The coding pipeline exists as a typed literal, is serialized to a committed and checksummed .bober/topology/coding.json, and `bober pge dump|validate|hash` operate on it without any executor in the module graph. The repository is shippable: typecheck, typecheck:tests, build and lint clean, full Vitest suite green, and the only user-visible change is a new `pge` subcommand that reads and writes topology data.
assumptions: The CLI verb is `bober pge` and the directory is .bober/topology/, because `bober graph` and .bober/graph/ are already the code-graph namespace (cli/commands/graph.ts:39). A thin `bober graph topology <verb>` alias may be added later; both rename cleanly now and expensively after the CI job exists.
graphVersion starts at 1.0.0 and is bumped by hand; the CI gate that enforces the bump lands in sprint 14.
The authored literal describes the pipeline agent-bober already runs imperatively, so it is a description of shipped behaviour rather than a proposal for new behaviour.
outOfScope: Documenting the nodes in docs/pge-graph.md — sprint 14.
generatorNotes: Register the command in src/cli/index.ts following the existing pattern used by cli/commands/graph.ts. Keep src/cli/commands/pge.ts thin: parse args, call into src/pge/topology/**, map ValidationReport to an exit code and a printed code name. The literal must carry, per node: id, kind, promptRef for llm nodes, effects[], modelTier, optional cache policy, inputPorts/outputPorts with schemaRef, writes/reads channel lists, and for routers a closed targets[] of {label,to}. Loop-bearing routers (research_route, sprint_route, rework_route) must each declare counterKey, maxIterations and onExhausted or sprint 1's UnboundedCycle rule will fire. Every supervisor-to-subgraph transition needs a gate node on both sides (gate_research_in/out, gate_plan_in/out, gate_sprint_in/out, gate_eval_in) or BoundaryNotGated fires. The fan-out edge from fanout_sprints targets the single sprint subgraph with runtime-determined cardinality, so the checksum stays invariant to contract count.
evaluatorNotes: Confirm .bober/topology/coding.json is committed to git and not ignored. Confirm the runtime-loads-JSON rule is respected in spirit: nothing outside src/pge/topology/ and the CLI imports coding.graph.ts. Verify the zero-execution assertion is a spy over the executor lookup path and not a tautology. Verify the two-model-configuration test genuinely varies resolved model ids rather than asserting on the same value twice. Confirm the mutated-artifact case for dump --check exits non-zero rather than silently rewriting the file.
